Hi IQT, 
If I intend to engage a Patent agent, preferably you,  after filing my provisional application, what if my reference numbering was not done absolutely correctly since I am inexperienced ? And what if I have minor issues like with Antecedents ? In other words, if the provisional application has minor typo or syntax or spelling issues or missing reference numbers for example, I forgot to label a reference number for an element except 99% of the time it is referenced ? How does these imperfections affect my provisional? I mean when my patent agent refers to this application for priority date, how will the examiners penalise such imperfections?

comments.author: @1stPrinciples455
comments.text:
Hi IQT,
I have a dilemma. I can describe clearly an embodiment which specific features. For example, a device uses a bolt to fasten together two sub members.

However, I am not sure is an embodiment Constraining the possible scope I should cover? 

Can I describe the embodiment using a bolt as fastener but in my claims section I use the generic term fastener without specifying the word bolt?

I mean, an embodiment to me is something specific. Something tangible and accompanied by a drawing. So I have to describe it clearly. But we know that not just the bolt can do the same job. A screw or rivet can achieve the same results, for example. So do I describe the embodiment in the detailed description section using the word fastener or do I specify clearly and then generically use only the word fastener in the claims?
